decision.expected_measurable_effect: After the changed controller (control/recipe/holding_tip_speed_weight = 0.05; terminal_tip_speed_weight unchanged at 0.0) is executed end-to-end in a complete simulation with unchanged reach evaluation and sampled holding/profile feedback, the final holding-window samples (F78 = 0.30-0.35 s, F81 = all recorded samples in final holding window, 6 rows F35/F38) should show sampled speed_m_s below the baseline range [F20 = 0.6351726092425104, F27 = 1.5810152739742807] m/s and closer to settling speed_limit_m_s = 0.02 m/s (F49), potentially flipping holding_speed_passed (F63) true, while terminal reach (F40; terminal_error_m F47 = 0.007642608585867386 m vs reach_tolerance_m F13 = 0.01 m) and holding position (late_max_error_m F10 = 0.05813810428573256 m vs position_limit_m F36 = 0.01 m) are re-measured in the same units and limits; mean_update_s (F44 = 17.26331904856488 s vs control_period_s F48 = 0.01 s) and deadline_misses (F16 = 35) are re-checked and should not increase materially. All reported quantities stay in the retained baseline units and limits; no raw scalar objective comparison across weights is made.
decision.rationale: Hypothesis (testable, explicitly not causal): the retained holding-speed failure is associated with holding_tip_speed_weight = 0.0 (F86) together with terminal_tip_speed_weight = 0.0 (F32). With no cost on tip speed at or after the scheduled settling-window start, the retained baseline keeps sampled tip speed in the final window at [F20 = 0.6351726092425104, F27 = 1.5810152739742807] m/s over 6 rows (F35, F38; window coverage F78 = 0.30-0.35 s, F81 = all recorded samples in final holding window) against settling speed_limit_m_s = 0.02 m/s (F49; F68), with terminal_speed_m_s = 0.6351726092425104 m/s (F30) and holding_speed_passed = false (F63), while reach passed (F40) with terminal_error_m = 0.007642608585867386 m (F47) inside reach_tolerance_m = 0.01 m (F13). Relevance: the editable holding term is precisely a per-second weight on squared spatial tip speed at nodes at or after the configured settling-window start, and the failed quantity is sampled spatial tip speed at those same nodes; the configuration supplies the explicit settling settings this term requires (window_s = 0.05, F65/F87; position_limit_m = 0.01, F36/F76; speed_limit_m_s = 0.02, F49/F68) and horizon = 10 (F43). Selection: adopt exactly one changed weight, control/recipe/holding_tip_speed_weight 0.0 -> 0.05 (legal: bounds [0,1], new positive >= 0.0001, nonempty effective delta). A moderate value is chosen because the observed violation is roughly 30-80x the limit (F20, F27 vs F49) and no computed cost-contribution scaling is retained (F31), so a near-minimum weight risks a null experiment while a large weight risks dominating the cost; the admissible range is [0,1] and no developer-prescribed value is used. terminal_tip_speed_weight is left at 0.0 (F32) so this bounded first experiment changes one variable only, avoiding confounding and a possible trade-off against the currently passing reach; the terminal speed cost remains a single terminal scaled squared-speed term with tip_speed_scale_m_s = 0.02 m/s (F32, F73), and the holding speed cost remains an integration-step-weighted sum at the scheduled holding nodes (F37, F65, F87) with scale and scheduling unchanged. All other fields are fixed. Expected effects, stated separately and hedged: (1) holding speed - primary target; the holding-window speed_m_s samples (F78, F35, F38) should move down from [F20, F27] toward 0.02 m/s (F49); (2) reach - should be retained at least as good as the retained pass (F40, F47 vs F13), though penalising speed at settling nodes can trade off position; (3) holding position - late_max_error_m (F10 = 0.05813810428573256 m; window maximum F57) versus 0.01 m (F36, F76) is the secondary quantity and could improve or worsen; (4) computation - mean_update_s (F44 = 17.26331904856488 s) versus control_period_s = 0.01 s (F48), deadline_misses (F16 = 35 of 35), stopping_counts (F18 = 1 Solve_Succeeded / F84 = 34 User_Requested_Stop), max_cpu_s = 30.0 s (F33) and max_iterations = 120 (F90) are expected to stay within the same order, since adding one quadratic term does not materially change solver size, but no budget change is assumed. Possible adverse effects: a heavier holding-speed penalty can reduce achievable tip motion and worsen holding position error (F10) or terminal error (F47); near the 0.05 s settling window (F65) the added term interacts with tracking_weight = 1.0 (F23), terminal_weight = 5.0 (F34), velocity_weight = 0.0001 (F79), terminal_velocity_weight = 0.0001 (F15), variation_weight = 0.001 (F4) and tension_weight = 0.0001 (F24); with near-deadline solves (F44 vs F48, F16) a heavier nonlinear cost could shift optimizer truncation behaviour (F18, F84, F69), and any torque consequence is bounded by force_limit_n = 8.0 N per tendon over 6 tendons. Observations that would weaken the hypothesis: a completed run with unchanged or higher holding-window speed (F20, F27, F78); a worsened holding position (F10) or reach (F47 vs F13); an unchanged terminal_speed_m_s (F30); or no measurable change in solver stopping/truncation behaviour, which would point toward the retained solver budget (F44, F16, F18, F84) rather than the absent speed weight. Boundaries: single retained execution with full_snapshots_available = false (F3); no closed-loop counterfactual replay or causal attribution and no retained warm plans or iteration traces (F14, F31); this is a bounded testable hypothesis, not a dominant-cause claim, and raw scalar objective values are not compared across weights - only the same retained sampled units and limits as the baseline. local_comparison omitted: source.controller_horizon was not queried in this context, so no saved baseline update with a verified effective horizon of 0.01 s can be named without guessing an update_id; per the grant, an unavailable or inconclusive screen does not prohibit this justified complete experiment.

terminal.definition: Euclidean world tip position error at the final execution sample; sealed evaluate.reach is the outcome authority.

duration.definition: Final closed interval [task duration - window, task duration].

position.definition: Maximum sampled world tip position error in the final interval.

speed.definition: Maximum sampled world tip translational speed norm in the final interval.

coverage.definition: Both endpoints, timestamps aligned to task sample_period_s; missing samples are unavailable, never a pass.

speed.definition: Euclidean norm of tip-site translational Jacobian times recorded backend qvel, reconstructed with sealed robot.xml and qpos; no finite differencing

control_period.definition: Simulated control spacing; synchronous wall overruns do not imply skipped applied updates or injected actuator delay.

duration.definition: Simulated task horizon, separate from computation wall time.

timing.interpretation: Applied updates, initialization selections, simulated duration and measured wall time are separate facts.

policy.computation: Reported separately; never substitutes for reach or holding acceptance.
policy.objective: Raw scalar objectives under different weights are not ranked.
policy.rule: Joint acceptance first; otherwise componentwise physical comparison.
policy.tradeoff: Any physical improvement accompanied by physical worsening is a trade-off, not overall improvement.

mapped.meaning: Dimensionless terminal weight on squared world tip speed / tip_speed_scale_m_s. Zero preserves legacy cost.

scaling.semantics: Squared world tip speed divided by speed scale squared; terminal node cost.

mapped.legal_domain: Schema nonnegative finite; reach builder requires zero or [0.0001, 1].
